doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Years at the Metropole with Shavers, Hawkins and others
summary: Marty's ten years at the Metropole with Charlie Shavers and Coleman Hawkins.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Right. Did you want to show us a few items from your book?
Any other bands you want to talk, or are we running out of time?

Oh boy that was great, I loved it. Guys would say to me, “why are you working that dump?” I said, “what do you mean, dump?” You know what I did at the Metropole? Well of course I worked with my own groups, I worked with other people, but I was there for about ten years, different people. And for approximately two and a half years I worked with Charlie Shavers, Coleman Hawkins, Mickey Sheen, and the bass players fluctuated, either Arvell Shaw or Benny Moten, different bass players. But with Charlie Shavers and Coleman Hawkins. And when Coleman took off, Roy Eldridge would play, and one night Charlie took off and he sent in Dizzy Gillespie. You know it was fantastic, man I loved it, it was just great. And it was just magnificent. Not only that, at that particular time all the country clubs around the New York metropolitan area would have like some Saturday night they would say why don’t we have a Dixieland theme, who can we get? Who is at the Metropole? I got called all the time. Because I would work, like for instance there was a guy, Tony Cabot was a society bandleader. First he worked with Meyer Davis, and then he split and he got his own office, and he used to use me all the time. I worked with Tony for 30 years. But anyway he would call me, and I would work with his band on the date, to do [scats] I would play the jobs because I knew all those things see? Now a lot of the jazz guys don’t. They know their jazz tunes and that’s it. So they’d get Marty, because now and then they would say okay but we want you to bring a couple of guys, because during the night we’re going to bring you out and let you play some Dixieland things.
